title.analysis: Authentic title "The Reasons Why Most Americans Are Broke" promises an explanatory list. The script delivers eleven behavioural reasons with remedies, but "most Americans are broke" is never quantified beyond the $400 statistic (which shows about a third, not most), and the script attributes being broke to behaviour while dismissing income without evidence.

script.analysis: Full 24921 canonical characters read. A single-narrator list essay with no composites: hook on observing spenders, the $400 emergency statistic, and eleven numbered reasons (no goals, no emergency fund, no spending plan, present focus, expensive habits with cigarette and dining figures, bad debt, status spending, not paying yourself first, fear of risk, single income stream, no ongoing financial education), then a remedies section and close. Mostly generic advice; the single statistic is overstated and the income-dismissal claim is unsupported.

claim_audit.assessment: Partly correct: the Fed SHED for 2024 (published May 2025) found 63% would cover $400 with cash or its equivalent, so 37% would not. But 'simply cannot cover it' overstates: most of that 37% would cover it by borrowing or selling something; only about 12-13% could not pay by any means.
